# rlimit

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/rlimit"
```

Package rlimit applies per\-process resource ceilings via setrlimit\(2\) / prlimit64\(2\).

It is the thin public facade over internal/service/proc/rlimit: the types are aliases of the core proc value types and the functions delegate straight to the service implementation. Resources are named abstractly \(Resource\) and mapped to the platform RLIMIT\_\* constant inside the service layer, so calling code stays portable; on a non\-Linux host every call returns the typed UnsupportedPlatform error rather than acting.

### Usage

Lower the open\-file ceiling of the current process to 1024 soft / 4096 hard:

```
import (
	"github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/rlimit"
)

err := rlimit.Apply(0, map[rlimit.Resource]rlimit.Limit{
	rlimit.ResourceNoFile: {Soft: 1024, Hard: 4096},
})
if err != nil {
	// inspect with errs.HasCode(err, ...) — RlimitFailed / UnknownResource.
}
```

A pid of 0 targets the calling process via setrlimit\(2\). Any other pid targets that process via prlimit64\(2\), which requires the CAP\_SYS\_RESOURCE capability; without it the call returns RlimitFailed wrapping EPERM.

### Spec integration

Go's os/exec SysProcAttr carries no rlimit field, so limits cannot be applied declaratively before exec. The honest model is: apply limits from the child after fork \(a pid\-0 Apply in the child\) or, when supervising, apply them to the spawned pid via prlimit64. PrepareSysProcAttr validates a limit set without any syscall — call it at Spec\-construction time to fail fast on a Resource this platform cannot honour, before a process is ever spawned.

### Platform notes

Only Linux is supported. RLIMIT\_NPROC and RLIMIT\_MEMLOCK are absent from Go's syscall package and are restated from the kernel generic ABI inside the service layer. Off Linux, Apply and PrepareSysProcAttr return UnsupportedPlatform.

## Constants

<a name="LimitInfinity"></a>LimitInfinity is the soft/hard value meaning "no limit" \(RLIM\_INFINITY\).

```go
const LimitInfinity uint64 = coreproc.LimitInfinity
```

<a name="Apply"></a>
## func [Apply](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/rlimit/rlimit.go#L98>)

```go
func Apply(pid int, limits map[Resource]Limit) error
```

Apply sets the soft/hard ceilings in limits on the process identified by pid. A pid of 0 targets the calling process; any other pid targets that process via prlimit64\(2\) and needs CAP\_SYS\_RESOURCE. It returns UnknownResource for an unmapped resource, RlimitFailed on a syscall failure, and UnsupportedPlatform off Linux.

<a name="PrepareSysProcAttr"></a>
## func [PrepareSysProcAttr](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/rlimit/rlimit.go#L108>)

```go
func PrepareSysProcAttr(limits map[Resource]Limit) error
```

PrepareSysProcAttr validates limits without issuing any syscall and reports whether they can be applied on this platform, returning the same typed errors Apply would \(UnknownResource / UnsupportedPlatform\). Use it to fail fast at Spec\-construction time; Go's SysProcAttr has no rlimit field, so the actual application happens post\-fork via Apply.

<a name="Limit"></a>
## type [Limit](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/rlimit/rlimit.go#L91>)

Limit is an immutable soft/hard setrlimit\(2\) pair. It aliases the core proc LimitValue type.

```go
type Limit = coreproc.LimitValue
```

<a name="Resource"></a>
## type [Resource](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/rlimit/rlimit.go#L87>)

Resource is the abstract, platform\-portable resource enum mapped to a RLIMIT\_\* constant by the service layer. It aliases the core proc type.

```go
type Resource = coreproc.Resource
```

<a name="ResourceAS"></a>ResourceAS limits the process virtual address\-space size \(RLIMIT\_AS\).

```go
const ResourceAS Resource = coreproc.ResourceAS
```

<a name="ResourceCPU"></a>ResourceCPU limits CPU time in seconds \(RLIMIT\_CPU\).

```go
const ResourceCPU Resource = coreproc.ResourceCPU
```

<a name="ResourceCore"></a>ResourceCore limits the core\-dump size in bytes \(RLIMIT\_CORE\).

```go
const ResourceCore Resource = coreproc.ResourceCore
```

<a name="ResourceData"></a>ResourceData limits the process data\-segment size \(RLIMIT\_DATA\).

```go
const ResourceData Resource = coreproc.ResourceData
```

<a name="ResourceFSize"></a>ResourceFSize limits the largest file the process may create \(RLIMIT\_FSIZE\).

```go
const ResourceFSize Resource = coreproc.ResourceFSize
```

<a name="ResourceMemLock"></a>ResourceMemLock limits bytes that may be locked into RAM \(RLIMIT\_MEMLOCK\).

```go
const ResourceMemLock Resource = coreproc.ResourceMemLock
```

<a name="ResourceNProc"></a>ResourceNProc limits the number of processes for the real uid \(RLIMIT\_NPROC\).

```go
const ResourceNProc Resource = coreproc.ResourceNProc
```

<a name="ResourceNoFile"></a>ResourceNoFile limits the highest open file descriptor \(RLIMIT\_NOFILE\). It re\-exports the core enum value so consumers qualify it as rlimit.ResourceNoFile.

```go
const ResourceNoFile Resource = coreproc.ResourceNoFile
```

<a name="ResourceStack"></a>ResourceStack limits the process stack size \(RLIMIT\_STACK\).

```go
const ResourceStack Resource = coreproc.ResourceStack
```
